program_name: Master in Environmental Management of Mountain Areas, universally abbreviated EMMA. The name is identical on the English, German, Italian and Ladin unibz pages — unibz does NOT translate it (the Italian nav also reads 'Master in Environmental Management of Mountain Areas'). The University of Innsbruck runs the same programme under the German title 'Masterstudium Umweltmanagement in Bergregionen' and the English title 'Environmental Management of Mountain Areas (EMMA)'. Delivered by the unibz Faculty of Agricultural, Environmental and Food Sciences (in 2019/20 it sat under the then Faculty of Science and Technology) 'in cooperation with the University of Innsbruck (Austria)' — on the Innsbruck side the Faculty of Biology (and historically also the Faculty of Engineering Science / Technische Wissenschaften). unibz's ranking-list index files it under the heading 'Inter-university Masters', alongside Energy Engineering, Industrial Mechanical Engineering and Food Sciences for Innovation and Authenticity. The unibz programme page's own strapline calls it a 'double degree programme'.
level: Master (Italian 'laurea magistrale', second-cycle degree, EQF/NQF level 7). 120 ECTS over 2 years / 4 semesters, degree class LM-73. Innsbruck classifies the award as 'Master of Science (MSc)', 'Master (Second Cycle)', level 7. Entry qualification is a bachelor degree; at enrolment the Diploma Supplement must show 'at least 180 credit points (ECTS)' and 'that the qualification gives access to a Master programme'. The degree opens access to PhD programmes — unibz runs a directly related doctorate, the PhD in Mountain Environment and Agriculture, and Innsbruck offers doctoral programmes in Biology. PROFESSIONAL NOTE: unibz's own 2019/20 Study Manifesto states 'The Master Programme prepares for the Italian professional qualification of "Agronomist and Forester"' — i.e. via the Italian state examination (esame di Stato) it leads towards Section A of the Ordine dei Dottori Agronomi e Dottori Forestali. [uncertain] This professional-qualification sentence appears in the 2019/20 manifesto and is NOT repeated in the 2026/27 brochure or admission-information PDF; it should be re-confirmed with the Faculty before being relied on.
teaching_language: FULLY ENGLISH-TAUGHT AT ENTRY AND FOR THE ENTIRE FIRST YEAR — this is NOT one of unibz's trilingual programmes. unibz brochure 'At a glance', verbatim: 'Courses will be taught in English'. unibz admission-information PDF, verbatim: 'The official teaching language is English.' The only admission language requirement is English B2; there is NO German and NO Italian requirement at entry or at graduation. IMPORTANT SECOND-YEAR NUANCE, visible only on the Innsbruck side: the University of Innsbruck's own EMMA page states 'The official teaching language is English. Elective compulsory subjects are offered in English, German or Italian.' unibz's own 2019/20 Study Manifesto said the same in older wording: 'The official teaching language is English. Optional courses will be offered in English, German or Italian', and listed 'Languages used in teaching: English (main language), German, Italian'. CONSEQUENCE: year 1 in Bolzano (60 ECTS of compulsory core courses) is entirely in English, but the year-2 elective menu at Innsbruck (23 ECTS of free-choice courses drawn from the Innsbruck Faculty of Biology catalogue) includes German-language options, so an English-only student has a NARROWER, not an empty, choice in Innsbruck. The one compulsory year-2 module and the thesis are English. WARNING ABOUT A MISLEADING FIELD: the Innsbruck programme database lists 'Language: German, English, Italian' and links a page called 'Language Certificates (German)'. That is Innsbruck's generic institutional metadata; it is NOT an EMMA-specific German entry requirement, because admission is run entirely by unibz, whose governing document requires only English B2. [uncertain] Exactly how many of the Innsbruck free-choice modules are guaranteed in English each year is not published; this is the single most important question an English-only applicant should put to the degree course director before accepting a place.
campus: TWO CITIES IN TWO COUNTRIES, one year in each. unibz brochure 'At a glance': 'Campus: Bozen-Bolzano and Innsbruck'. YEAR 1 — Free University of Bozen-Bolzano, main campus, Universitätsplatz 1 / piazza Università 1, 39100 Bozen-Bolzano, Italy (Faculty of Agricultural, Environmental and Food Sciences). Verbatim: 'The first year must be completed at the Free University of Bozen-Bolzano and is organised in compulsory core courses (60 ECTS) for all students divided between the two semesters.' YEAR 2 — University of Innsbruck, Austria, specifically the Faculty of Biology: 'The second year at the University of Innsbruck, with one compulsory module and several elective modules...' The brochure's study plan is explicit that year 2 sits '(at Faculty of Biology, University of Innsbruck)'. THESIS — location is the student's choice: '30 CP Thesis (at either Free University of Bozen-Bolzano or University of Innsbruck)'; 'The degree can be successfully concluded after the elaboration and defense of an original thesis work, which can be performed at either universities.' PRACTICAL GEOGRAPHY: Bolzano and Innsbruck are about 120 km apart across the Brenner Pass, roughly 2 hours by train or car; both are Alpine cities, and the programme 'takes advantage of the particular location of the partner universities in the Central Alps'. This is a genuine RELOCATION, not a commute: the student moves country, housing, bank and (for non-EU citizens) immigration status between year 1 and year 2. ATTENDANCE ASYMMETRY (brochure, verbatim): 'There is no compulsory attendance at unibz, although attendance of lessons, exercise classes and lab work is strongly recommended. Attendance is instead compulsory for part of the courses offered at the University of Innsbruck.' NOT a NOI Techpark, Brixen-Bressanone or Bruneck-Brunico programme.
degree_class: LM-73 — 'Scienze e tecnologie forestali ed ambientali' (Forest and Environmental Sciences and Technologies), the Italian ministerial second-cycle degree class. Stated verbatim in the brochure 'At a glance' ('Degree class: LM-73'), on the programme page, and in the header of the signed 2026/27 ranking list ('Admission to the Master in Environmental Management of Mountain Areas (LM-73)'). It is the natural second cycle above the Italian bachelor class L-25 (Agriculture and Forestry), which is precisely why the entry requirements are written in terms of L-25 credit sectors. PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCES: (1) double-enrolment rule, verbatim from the admission PDF — 'you can enrol in a maximum of two programmes simultaneously, provided that they do not belong to the same class (e.g. LM-73 and LM-73) and differ in at least two-thirds of their content'; (2) LM-73 is the class Italian professional bodies map to the forestry/agronomy profession, relevant for later registration in Section A of the Ordine dei Dottori Agronomi e Dottori Forestali after the state examination. NOTE ON A MISLEADING FILENAME: unibz's archived 2019/20 manifesto is served at a URL containing 'LM33' ('Manifesto-2019-06-07-Master-EMMA-LM33-en.pdf'), but the document body itself states 'Degree class LM-73' and 'Master class: LM-73'. The 'LM33' in the filename is a unibz filing error, not a former classification.

is_new_programme: NOT a new programme — EMMA is one of the longest-running English-taught masters at unibz. FOUNDED: launched in AUTUMN 2014 as a jointly designed Bozen–Innsbruck double-degree master, with 35 study places, per the University of Innsbruck's own 2014 press release announcing the 'new' programme. It has therefore been running for roughly twelve intakes. EVIDENCE OF MATURITY: (a) unibz publishes a 'Percentage grade distribution LM-73' page showing not only a full exam-grade distribution but a distribution of FINAL GRADUATION grades — 110 cum laude 38.64%, 110 without honours 31.82%, with grades 98–109 spread thinly at 2.27–9.09% each — i.e. many cohorts have already graduated, and graduated extremely well; (b) a named Student Representative sits on the Course Council (Mackenzie Robin Walker); (c) unibz links AlmaLaurea graduate-satisfaction and employability statistics for the programme. STRUCTURAL EVOLUTION, worth knowing: in 2019/20 the programme had 30 EU + 5 non-EU places, tuition of EUR 1,347.50, an admission procedure of 'Academic qualification and eventual interview', and TWO curricula ('Sustainable mountain agriculture and development' and 'Environmental protection'). By 2026/27 it has 45 EU + 8 non-EU places, EUR 1,200 tuition, no interview at all, and a single study plan. It also moved faculty, from the Faculty of Science and Technology to the Faculty of Agricultural, Environmental and Food Sciences. So the programme is old but has been materially reshaped — and consistently in the direction of being LARGER and EASIER to apply to.
majors_tracks_study_plans: ONE SINGLE STUDY PLAN in the current structure — no majors, no tracks, no curriculum choice at application, and therefore no separate quotas or admission codes. This is a simplification from the past: the 2019/20 manifesto ran TWO curricula, 'Sustainable mountain agriculture and development' and 'Environmental protection', each with its own year-1 course list. Only the second survives; the unibz German-language navigation still labels the current plan 'Study Plan Environmental Protection' and pairs it with 'Angebotene Lehrveranstaltungen - eingeschrieben vom 2021' (course offering for students enrolled from 2021), indicating the single-plan structure took effect with the 2021 intake. WHERE THE REAL CHOICE LIES — YEAR 2 AT INNSBRUCK. Year 1 (60 ECTS at unibz) is 100% compulsory core, identical for everyone: Environmental data analysis (3 CP); Mountain hydrology and risk processes (6 CP = Natural risk in mountain areas: processes and mitigation strategies 3 + Experimental river hydraulics 3); Basics of landscape ecology and ecosystem restoration (6 CP); Management of forests and agricultural resources in mountain areas (9 CP = Management of mountain forests 6 + Management of agricultural resources 3); Forest ecophysiology and soil ecology (6 CP = Tree physiology and climate change 3 + Soil ecology 3); Management of mountain rivers (6 CP = Hydro-morphology of mountain rivers 3 + Flood risk mitigation in mountain rivers 3); Advanced geomatics and environmental impact assessment (6 CP = Advanced geomatics 3 + Environmental impact assessment 3); Forest planning and harvesting (6 CP = Forest inventory 3 + Forest harvesting and logistics 3); Nature conservation and management (6 CP = Grassland and alpine vegetation ecology and management 3 + Nature conservation and protected areas 3); Advanced ecological restoration and protection forestry (6 CP = Advanced restoration ecology and ecosystem restoration 3 + Protection forestry and natural hazards 3). Year 2 (60 ECTS at the Innsbruck Faculty of Biology) is where specialisation happens: '23 CP Free Choice Courses', '7 CP Selected Topics in Environmental Management (one mandatory course)', '30 CP Thesis'. unibz describes the effective specialisation directions as 'environmental and resource management, nature protection, landscape ecology and planning, agriculture as well as water management in mountain areas'. Innsbruck's own EMMA course page describes the same year differently — a compulsory module 'CM1: Current Aspects in Environmental Management' (7.5 ECTS, seminar plus project study), roughly 22.5 ECTS of elective modules chosen from about nine options (Water and Sediment Management, Natural Hazard Management, Advanced Landscape Ecology, Biodiversity and others), and a Master's thesis of 28 ECTS, with most courses concentrated in the winter (3rd) semester. 'Every year the Faculty publishes the list of free choice courses offered.' [uncertain] The two universities publish DIFFERENT year-2 credit splits (unibz 7 + 23 + 30 = 60; Innsbruck 7.5 + 22.5 + 28 = 58) and Innsbruck's overview page says 'two compulsory modules' while unibz says 'one compulsory module'. These are unreconciled on both sites; the authoritative year-2 breakdown should be requested from the Faculty. NO OTHER VARIANTS: no dual-study/apprenticeship model, no part-time route, no additional double degrees beyond Innsbruck, and no compulsory internship ('This study programme does not involve a compulsory internship'), though voluntary internships and thesis periods abroad can be arranged, and unibz offers exchange programmes with partner universities worldwide.
english_only_accessibility: PARTIALLY OPEN — genuinely open at admission and for all of year 1, with a real but manageable narrowing in year 2. WHY IT IS OPEN: (a) the sole language requirement is English B2 ('Entry level (to gain admission) English: B2'); (b) there is NO German and NO Italian requirement at entry, NO third-language B1 threshold, and NO exit/graduation language requirement — this is an English-taught, not a trilingual, programme; (c) the whole application is in English and needs no motivation letter, video, portfolio or interview; (d) year 1 in Bolzano is 60 ECTS of compulsory core courses taught in English, so an English-only student has zero curricular exposure risk in the first year; (e) the thesis can be written and defended in English at either university; (f) the competition data are unusually friendly — see places_quotas. WHY IT IS NOT FULLY OPEN: (i) YEAR 2 ELECTIVES. Innsbruck states 'Elective compulsory subjects are offered in English, German or Italian', and 23 ECTS of year 2 are free-choice courses from the Innsbruck Faculty of Biology catalogue. An English-only student will have a smaller menu than a German-speaking one. This is a curricular-choice constraint, not a graduation barrier — the compulsory module and thesis are English — but it is the single most important thing to verify before accepting a place. (ii) DAILY LIFE IN INNSBRUCK. Bolzano is officially bilingual German/Italian with an English-friendly university environment; Innsbruck is a monolingual German-speaking Austrian city, and administration, housing and part-time work there run in German. Year 2 is a harder daily-life environment for an English-only student than year 1. (iii) FIELD AND EXCURSION WORK in South Tyrolean forestry and agriculture often involves German/Italian-speaking practitioners. (iv) THE REAL FILTER IS ACADEMIC, NOT LINGUISTIC: the 20 + 30 ECTS credit thresholds in the L-25 subject sectors (see academic_requirements) are what actually exclude applicants, together with the 22/30-equivalent grade floor implied by the 55/95 threshold. In the 2026/27 Early Bird round, only 4 of about 37 EU applicants were excluded for failing requirements or the score, while 2 were excluded on language. FOR A TURKISH APPLICANT specifically: an Orman Mühendisliği, Ziraat Mühendisliği, Peyzaj Mimarlığı, Çevre Mühendisliği or Biyoloji background with an English-medium degree faces no language obstacle at admission whatsoever, and the non-EU competition is mild. The two things to plan for are the year-2 Innsbruck elective language question and the Austrian immigration step (see non_eu_visa_process).
admission_type: RESTRICTED ACCESS (numero programmato / limited places), decided by a purely DOCUMENT-BASED, FORMULA-DRIVEN ranking. There is NO entrance exam, NO TOLC, NO SAT, NO GRE/GMAT, NO portfolio, NO motivation letter, NO video presentation and — unlike almost every other unibz master — NO INTERVIEW. This is one of the simplest admission procedures at unibz. Mechanics, verbatim from the admission-information PDF and the signed ranking list: 'If the number of eligible applicants exceeds the maximum number of available places (see section "Available places"), you will be assessed for admission based on your academic qualifications. The Admission Committee can assign up to a max. of 95 points based on the: final bachelor grade expressed out of 30 (for applicants already graduated); weighted grade average expressed out of 30 (for applicants not graduated yet). The Admission Committee will assign 2 points to candidates who graduated with honors (cum laude). Candidates who possess at least a C1 certificate in the official teaching language of the course (English) will be assigned 3 points. Minimum score for admission is 55/95 points.' So the components are exactly four: (1) an ELIGIBILITY CHECK on the entry qualification / L-25 credit thresholds; (2) a LANGUAGE GATE at English B2 — failure means exclusion from the admission procedure regardless of grade (2 EU applicants were excluded on this ground in the 2026/27 Early Bird round); (3) an ARITHMETIC SCORE derived from the bachelor grade, plus 2 for cum laude and plus 3 for a C1 English certificate; (4) a HARD THRESHOLD of 55/95, below which a candidate is excluded even if places remain (2 EU applicants fell here in Early Bird 2026/27). A MANDATORY STRUCTURED EXCEL FILE must be uploaded ('Please use the file available in the application portal'). Applications go through the unibz Application Portal at https://aws.unibz.it/exup. TIE-BREAK, in order: 'If scores are equal, applicants who have already graduated take precedence over applicants who have not graduated yet. In the event of further equal score, the younger applicant will be given priority (art. 3 L. 127/1997).' HISTORICAL CHANGE: the 2019/20 manifesto listed the procedure as 'Academic qualification and eventual interview' with fixed interview windows (6–10 May and 3–4 September 2019). The interview has since been abolished; no interview appears anywhere in the 2026/27 documents.
academic_requirements:
FOUR ALTERNATIVE QUALIFICATION ROUTES (admission-information PDF and signed ranking list, identical wording): '1. an adequate knowledge of the basic disciplines of Mathematics, Chemistry and Biology and fundamental knowledge of the subjects preparatory to the fundamental disciplines of this degree class. 2. a bachelor degree in the Italian degree class L-25 (Agriculture and Forestry) ex D.M. 270/2004 or equivalent qualification gained abroad. 3. a bachelor degree in biology of the partner University Innsbruck. 4. another Italian or foreign degree if you certify the following ECTS credit points: 20 credit points in the scientific sectors of the fundamental subjects ("attività di base") of the class L-25 (Agriculture and Forestry), and 30 credit points in the scientific sectors of the typical subjects ("attività caratterizzanti") of the class L-25 (Agriculture and Forestry), related at least to two different subject areas.'

ROUTE 4 IS THE ONE MOST FOREIGN APPLICANTS ARE ASSESSED AGAINST, and it is far LOOSER than the equivalent grids at unibz's engineering masters: only 50 ECTS in total (20 'attività di base' + 30 'attività caratterizzanti'), against for example 85 ECTS across three separate blocks for the Master in Energy Engineering. Note also the diversity condition attached to the 30: 'related at least to two different subject areas'.

CRITICAL DIFFERENCE FROM OTHER UNIBZ MASTERS — NO SSD CODE LIST IS PUBLISHED. Unlike Energy Engineering or Software Engineering, the EMMA documents do NOT enumerate the qualifying scientific-disciplinary sectors (neither the new post-2024-reform codes such as AGRI-xx/x, BIOS-xx/x, CEAR-xx/x nor the old AGR/xx, BIO/xx, ICAR/xx codes). Instead unibz outsources the judgement to human assessment and tells applicants to ask: 'For details about the required ECTS credit points, please contact the Faculty Secretariat at agriculture@unibz.it.' The reference frame is the ministerial table for the Italian bachelor class L-25 (Agriculture and Forestry), whose 'attività di base' are the mathematics/physics/informatics, chemistry and biology foundation areas and whose 'attività caratterizzanti' are the agronomic, forestry, animal-production, agricultural-engineering, agricultural-economics and land/environment areas. PRACTICAL IMPLICATION: an applicant cannot self-verify eligibility from the published documents; contacting the Faculty Secretariat and the degree course director BEFORE applying is effectively mandatory, and unibz says so twice.

FOREIGN QUALIFICATIONS, verbatim: 'Please note: The correspondence of credit points awarded abroad to scientific-disciplinary sectors will be based on the contents of the exams. Please contact the degree course director in case you graduated abroad.' The ranking list repeats: 'If you have graduated abroad, the correspondence of credit points awarded to scientific sectors will be based on the contents of the exams passed during your previous study career.' And: 'The Faculty reserves the right to request a description of the contents of the courses and/or teaching hours where necessary.' So syllabi/course descriptions should be prepared in advance.

A REMEDIAL ROUTE IS EXPLICITLY OFFERED — unusual and valuable. If you lack the 20/30 credits, the admission text points to unibz single-subject enrolment: 'You can enrol as external student through the following link: https://www.unibz.it/en/applicants/single-subject-courses/ and hand in the requested documents in the Student Office.' This lets a candidate close a credit gap at unibz itself before re-applying in a later cycle.

MINIMUM GRADE: no separate minimum average is stated in words (there is no '22/30' sentence as in the engineering masters). However, the 55/95 threshold functions as one — see selection_scoring, where the published score data imply that 55/95 corresponds exactly to a bachelor grade/weighted average of 22/30.

NOT YET GRADUATED: 'Applicants who do not yet have the required three-year degree may apply, but they must have the qualification by the enrolment deadline at the latest. Otherwise, they will be excluded from the procedure.' No minimum-ECTS-so-far condition is imposed (no '≥120 ECTS' rule as in some unibz masters).

AT ENROLMENT the Diploma Supplement must state 'that you have achieved at least 180 credit points (ECTS)' and 'that the qualification gives access to a Master programme'.

DOUBLE-ENROLMENT RULE: maximum two simultaneous programmes, which must not share a class (LM-73/LM-73) and 'must differ in at least two-thirds of their content'.

READING FOR A TURKISH APPLICANT: an Orman Mühendisliği (forestry engineering), Ziraat Mühendisliği (agricultural engineering), Peyzaj Mimarlığı (landscape architecture), Çevre Mühendisliği (environmental engineering), Biyoloji or Su Ürünleri background will normally clear route 4 without difficulty, since Turkish four-year programmes in these fields carry far more than 50 ECTS in the relevant areas. Weaker fits are pure Coğrafya, Şehir ve Bölge Planlama, İnşaat Mühendisliği or Kimya, where the 30 'attività caratterizzanti' credits across two different subject areas are the hurdle. Because no SSD list is published, a Turkish applicant should e-mail agriculture@unibz.it with an English transcript and course descriptions well before the application window opens.
entry_exam_or_test:
NO ENTRANCE EXAM OF ANY KIND — this is one of the very few unibz programmes with no test and no interview at all. Specifically absent: no unibz admission test; no TOLC (TOLC-I, TOLC-E or TOLC-S); no CENT-S; no SAT, GRE or GMAT and no GMAT/GRE bonus; no subject test; no oral interview (contrast the Master in Energy Engineering, whose non-EU applicants faced a 'mandatory interview'); no portfolio review; no video presentation. Admission is decided purely on uploaded documents plus an arithmetic score.

THE ONLY EXAM AN APPLICANT MIGHT SIT is the ENGLISH LANGUAGE PROFICIENCY EXAM at the unibz Language Centre, and only if they cannot prove B2 English by medium of instruction or by a recognised certificate. It is held ONLINE. 2026/27 sittings and their registration windows, verbatim: Early Bird — '16/03/2026 (registration: 02 - 09/03/2026) and 16 - 17 and 20 - 21/04/2026 (registration: 24/03 - 08/04/2026)'; Late — '22 - 26/06/2026 (registration: 28/05 - 15/06/2026) and 27/07 (registration: 10 - 19/07/2026)'. PROCEDURAL TRAP, verbatim: 'If you start your application outside a language exams registration period, you must return to the portal during one of the periods indicated above in order to register for an exam.'

HISTORICAL NOTE: an interview did once exist. The 2019/20 Study Manifesto lists the admission procedure as 'Academic qualification and eventual interview' with published windows ('1st Session: between 6 and 10 May 2019; 2nd Session: between 3 and 4 September 2019'). It has been removed from the current procedure and appears nowhere in the 2026/27 admission-information PDF, brochure or signed ranking list.
selection_scoring:
A SINGLE ARITHMETIC FORMULA, no rubric of subjective components. Verbatim (admission-information PDF and signed ranking list, identical): 'The Admission Committee can assign up to a max. of 95 points based on the: final bachelor grade expressed out of 30 (for applicants already graduated); weighted grade average expressed out of 30 (for applicants not graduated yet). The Admission Committee will assign 2 points to candidates who graduated with honors (cum laude). Candidates who possess at least a C1 certificate in the official teaching language of the course (English) will be assigned 3 points. Minimum score for admission is 55/95 points. If scores are equal, applicants who have already graduated take precedence over applicants who have not graduated yet. In the event of further equal score, the younger applicant will be given priority (art. 3 L. 127/1997).'

SO THE SCORE HAS ONLY THREE INPUTS: the bachelor grade (or weighted average if still studying), converted to a base out of 95; +2 for cum laude; +3 for C1-or-better English. Nothing else counts — not the CV, not work experience, not research, not the university's reputation, not a motivation letter. This makes EMMA one of the most mechanically predictable admissions at unibz: a candidate can compute their own score before applying.

DERIVED CONVERSION FORMULA (this is an INFERENCE from the published scores, not a published rule, but it fits every single data point). EMMA is unusual in that its ranking list PUBLISHES INDIVIDUAL SCORES. Across the 2026/27 Early Bird lists (31 EU + 9 non-EU entries) every observed score is either a multiple of 5 (65, 75, 80, 85, 90, 95) or a multiple of 5 plus 3 (68, 78, 83, 88, 93, 98). The +3 is plainly the C1 English bonus. The base values fit exactly the linear map base = 5 × (grade out of 30) − 55, i.e. each whole grade point is worth 5 points: grade 22/30 → 55, 24 → 65, 26 → 75, 27 → 80, 28 → 85, 29 → 90, 30 → 95. Note the elegant confirmation: the published minimum of 55/95 maps precisely to a bachelor grade of 22/30 — the same 22/30 floor unibz states explicitly in its engineering masters. PRACTICAL RULE OF THUMB THEREFORE: you need roughly a 22/30 Italian-scale weighted average to be eligible at all, and a C1 English certificate is worth the equivalent of 0.6 of a grade point. No score of 97, 100, 92 or 87 appears, so no cum laude bonus was awarded in this cohort (or it is folded into the base). [uncertain] This formula is derived, not published; treat it as a strong working model, not an official rule.

OBSERVED 2026/27 EARLY BIRD SCORE DISTRIBUTION. EU/parity, 31 admitted: 98, 98, 98, 95, 95, 95, 93, 93, 93, 93, 90, 90, 90, 90, 90, 88, 88, 85, 85, 85, 83, 83, 83, 80, 80, 80, 80, 78, 75, 68, 65. Non-EU living abroad, 8 admitted: 88, 83, 78, 78, 78, 78, 78, 68; waiting list rank 9: 68.

EFFECTIVE CUT-OFFS FOR 2026/27 EARLY BIRD: EU/parity — NONE beyond the 55 threshold. 31 applicants were admitted against 35 places, so the list did not fill and every eligible applicant got in; the lowest admitted score was 65 (≈ grade 24/30, no C1). Non-EU living abroad — the cut-off was 68 (≈ grade 24/30 with a C1 certificate), with one further applicant on 68 pushed onto the waiting list by the tie-break (already-graduated first, then younger). Strikingly, seven of the eight admitted non-EU applicants scored 78 or 88, i.e. almost all held C1 English.

STRATEGIC READING: (1) Because the score is 100% grade-driven, an applicant with a modest GPA cannot compensate with experience, publications or a strong letter — there is nowhere to put them. (2) Conversely, a strong GPA plus a C1 certificate essentially guarantees a top-quartile rank. (3) The C1 bonus is cheap and decisive at the margin: at the 2026/27 non-EU cut-off of 68, the +3 was exactly the difference between the last admitted score and a base of 65. Any non-EU applicant should obtain a C1-level certificate (IELTS 7.0+, TOEFL iBT 95+, Cambridge C1 Advanced), or better still document that their bachelor was English-medium — which unibz recognises AS C1 and therefore also earns the +3, at no cost. (4) The tie-break rewards having already graduated, which argues for applying in the cycle after graduation rather than in the final undergraduate year, where places are contested.
bonus_points:
ONLY ONE TRUE BONUS EXISTS, plus one honours adjustment. (1) C1 ENGLISH BONUS — verbatim: 'Candidates who possess at least a C1 certificate in the official teaching language of the course (English) will be assigned 3 points.' Worth 3 of a 95-point scale, and demonstrably decisive at the non-EU margin in 2026/27 (cut-off 68 = base 65 + 3). CRUCIALLY, this bonus can be earned WITHOUT sitting any exam: unibz recognises an English-medium high-school final year and an English-medium bachelor or master degree 'as C1'. A Turkish applicant from a 100%-English-medium programme who uploads a registrar's medium-of-instruction letter should therefore receive the 3 points at zero cost. Applicants from 30%-English Turkish programmes cannot rely on this and should sit IELTS/TOEFL to C1 level. (2) CUM LAUDE ADJUSTMENT — 'The Admission Committee will assign 2 points to candidates who graduated with honors (cum laude).' This applies to Italian-style 'con lode' graduations; whether and how a Turkish 'yüksek onur derecesi' or a first-class-equivalent distinction is mapped to it is not stated. No score in the published 2026/27 lists shows evidence of a +2 having been applied.

WHAT DOES NOT EXIST HERE, contrary to other unibz programmes: NO Webometrics university-ranking bonus (that is Software Engineering and Computing for Data Science, 3/2/1 points for a top-1000 / 1001-2000 / 2001-3000 university) — a bachelor from a highly ranked university earns EMMA applicants nothing; NO GMAT/GRE bonus (Accounting and Finance); NO startup-project presentation bonus (Entrepreneurship and Innovation, 30 points); NO video-presentation points (Energy Engineering, 10 points); NO CV or professional-experience points (Energy Engineering, 50 points). Work experience, publications, internships, ERASMUS periods and reference letters are formally worth ZERO in the EMMA ranking. This is a genuinely grade-only competition.
portfolio_and_materials:
NO PORTFOLIO, NO MOTIVATION LETTER, NO VIDEO, NO REFERENCE LETTERS, NO RESEARCH PROPOSAL — and, notably, NOT EVEN A CV. The EMMA application is the leanest at unibz. The admission-information PDF lists exactly three uploads under 'In the application portal, you must upload': '1. Qualification ... 2. Excel file: Please use the file available in the application portal. 3. English language certifications (at least of level B2)' — plus the valid ID card or passport required at account creation.

(1) QUALIFICATION EVIDENCE, verbatim: 'if graduated in Italy: diploma supplement or self-declaration (following the Italian D.P.R. no. 445/2000) of the degree awarded with the final grade and passed exams (if graduated) or, if not graduated yet, a certificate listing the exams passed; if graduated abroad: diploma supplement or final degree certificate with the passed exams (if graduated) or transcript of records (if not graduated yet) in Italian, German or English.' Mandatory contents: 'final grade, passed exams with indication of grade and date of passing, credit points, scientific fields (the latter only for Italian titles). For qualifications obtained abroad, also: scale of grades awarded by the university of provenance (with a minimum final grade to obtain the qualification and a maximum final grade achievable).' THIS LAST ITEM IS THE MOST COMMONLY OMITTED AND MOST DAMAGING OMISSION for foreign applicants: since the entire ranking is computed from the grade, unibz must know the scale. A Turkish applicant must supply an official statement of the grading scale (e.g. 4.00 maximum, 2.00 minimum to graduate) — ideally the registrar's grading-system page of the transcript, not a self-written note.

(2) THE EXCEL FILE — the structured study-career template downloaded from and re-uploaded to the application portal, in which the applicant maps their own exams onto the L-25 credit sectors. EMMA's own text does not spell out a knock-out clause, but sister unibz programmes state that applications without a completed Excel file are not considered, and it is the instrument the Committee uses to verify the 20 + 30 ECTS thresholds. Treat it as mandatory and decisive.

(3) ENGLISH LANGUAGE CERTIFICATION at B2 or above, or medium-of-instruction documentation, or registration for a unibz Language Centre exam. Administrative form: 'In case your final certificate has been awarded by an Italian public institution, you need to submit a self-declaration. In case your final certificate has been awarded by a foreign public institution, you need to upload diploma scanned copy of the original.'

(4) ID: 'You need to create an account and upload a valid ID card or passport (front/back). Please note: if your document is invalid, incomplete or unreadable, you will be excluded from the admission procedure.'

(5) FOR FOREIGN QUALIFICATIONS ALSO THE DIPLOMA: 'If you gained your qualification abroad, you must also upload the diploma of your qualification: if you are not yet in possession of the diploma, you'll need to upload it upon enrolment.'

(6) FOR PARITY-OF-TREATMENT APPLICANTS: a copy of the valid Italian permesso di soggiorno (or the renewal request if expired).

OPTIONAL BUT STRONGLY ADVISED, though not listed: course syllabi/descriptions, because 'The Faculty reserves the right to request a description of the contents of the courses and/or teaching hours where necessary.'

FORMAT LIMITS: unibz publishes NO file-size cap, page limit or word limit for EMMA (contrast the 20 MB PDF portfolio cap in the Design programmes or the 3-minute video in Energy Engineering). There is nothing to write and nothing to design — only documents to obtain.

HARD RULES: 'Once the application has been sent, it cannot be modified. Filled-in forms which have not been sent correctly will not be taken into consideration.' And, stated twice: 'Mendacious declarations will be criminally prosecuted and will result in the automatic exclusion from the ranking list.'
interview:
NO INTERVIEW. This is a defining feature of EMMA's admission and a genuine advantage over comparable unibz masters. The 2026/27 admission-information PDF, the 2026/27 brochure and the signed 2026/27 Early Bird ranking list contain no reference to an interview, a colloquium, a videoconference, an oral assessment or a convocation of any kind — the word does not appear. The Admission Committee decides on uploaded documents alone, using the 95-point arithmetic formula. There is likewise no 'adequacy of personal preparation' interview clause of the kind the Master in Energy Engineering operates, and no exclusion ground for non-attendance (contrast Energy Engineering, whose non-EU Early Bird list excluded applicants who 'did not participate in the mandatory interview').

CONSEQUENCE FOR APPLICANTS: nothing needs to be prepared, rehearsed or scheduled after submission, and there is no time-zone or connectivity risk for overseas candidates. It also means there is NO opportunity to explain or rescue a weak transcript — the grade is the application.

HISTORICAL: an interview did exist in earlier cycles. The 2019/20 Study Manifesto records the admission procedure as 'Academic qualification and eventual interview' with published windows of 6–10 May 2019 (1st session) and 3–4 September 2019 (2nd session). It has since been abolished. [uncertain] No unibz document states when or why the interview was dropped; a candidate should still confirm on the current-cycle admission PDF, since unibz can reinstate procedural elements from year to year.
conditional_admission:
YES — conditional (provisional) admission for not-yet-graduated applicants is explicitly available, and the rules are unusually generous in one respect and strict in another.

THE RULE, verbatim: 'Applicants who do not yet have the required three-year degree may apply, but they must have the qualification by the enrolment deadline at the latest. Otherwise, they will be excluded from the procedure. Proof of possession of the qualification must be provided by the enrolment deadline.' The ranking list adds: 'Until your graduation, you will be admitted conditionally. You must have achieved your degree by the enrolment deadline, otherwise you will be excluded' and 'applicants who have not concluded their bachelor's degree are provisionally admitted: requirement for admission is the conclusion of the bachelor studies by the enrolment deadline (13 October 2026, 12 midday)'.

GENEROUS ASPECT — NO MINIMUM-CREDIT CONDITION. Unlike several unibz masters (which require ≥120 ECTS already earned, or ≥140 for Data Analytics for Economics and Management), EMMA imposes NO threshold of credits earned so far. Any enrolled bachelor student may apply. Their score is computed from the 'weighted grade average expressed out of 30' instead of the final grade.

STRICT ASPECT — THE TIE-BREAK PENALISES YOU. 'If scores are equal, applicants who have already graduated take precedence over applicants who have not graduated yet.' In an oversubscribed round, a not-yet-graduated applicant loses every tie. In the 2026/27 non-EU round, where two applicants tied on 68 for the last place, this rule (or the subsequent age rule) decided who was admitted and who went onto the waiting list.

DEADLINE FOR 2026/27: graduation must be completed by 13 October 2026, 12:00 midday.

SAFETY VALVE, verbatim: 'Advice: If you achieve your qualification after the enrolment deadline, you should not pay the tuition fees to confirm the study place. You will be able to submit a late enrolment request and, only if there are study places still available, you can enrol by 11 December 2026.' The ranking list specifies the late enrolment request goes 'to the Rector'.

A SECOND, SEPARATE RESERVATION applies to foreign degrees: 'Applicants with qualifications gained abroad who have not uploaded their diploma are provisionally admitted until their study title can be verified' and 'Your admission will be under reservation until the above-mentioned documents are uploaded... If the access title is deemed eligible, the reservation will be lifted. Otherwise, enrolment will not be possible and you will be excluded.' A THIRD applies to all non-EU citizens living abroad: 'All non-EU citizens living abroad are provisionally admitted: requirement is the official communication sent by the Italian consulate abroad directly to unibz.'

FINAL WARNING: 'If you have been admitted in the ranking list, but you do not possess a valid admission qualification, you can be excluded with Rector's decree even after enrolment.'

[uncertain] Unlike some unibz ranking lists, the EMMA 2026/27 list does not asterisk individual provisionally-admitted applicants in a way that can be read from the extracted text, so the proportion of not-yet-graduated admits in this cohort cannot be quantified.
ofa_rules:
NOT APPLICABLE. OFA (obblighi formativi aggiuntivi / additional learning requirements) is an Italian instrument reserved for FIRST-CYCLE, open-access programmes where an applicant fails a compulsory entrance test; at unibz it is used in the Bachelor in Economics and Management, the Bachelor in Economics, Politics and Ethics and the Bachelor in Tourism, Sport and Event Management, all tied to a mathematics test. EMMA is a restricted-access SECOND-CYCLE programme with no entrance test, so the instrument cannot apply. Neither the 2026/27 admission-information PDF, the brochure, nor the signed 2026/27 ranking list mentions OFA, additional learning requirements, remedial obligations or credit debts, and the ranking list carries no OFA markers.

ITALIAN LAW DOES NOT PERMIT master-level admission with curricular credit debts to be settled after enrolment: the 20 + 30 ECTS thresholds in the L-25 sectors must be satisfied BEFORE admission. EMMA's functional equivalent of a remedial route therefore sits entirely on the pre-admission side, and unibz names it explicitly in the entry-requirements section: single-subject / external-student enrolment ('You can enrol as external student through the following link: https://www.unibz.it/en/applicants/single-subject-courses/ and hand in the requested documents in the Student Office'). A candidate short of the required credits takes single courses — at unibz or elsewhere — closes the gap, and applies in a subsequent cycle.
language_requirements:
ONE REQUIREMENT ONLY: ENGLISH AT B2 (CEFR) FOR ADMISSION. Verbatim: 'The official teaching language is English. Therefore, the following language requirements apply, otherwise you will be excluded from the admission procedure: Entry level (to gain admission) English: B2. The levels of the Common European Framework of Reference apply.'

There is NO German requirement, NO Italian requirement, NO third-language B1 threshold and NO graduation/exit language requirement. This holds even though the second year is spent in a German-speaking country: admission is governed entirely by unibz, and Innsbruck imposes no separate language admission of its own ('The admission to the study programme takes place by the rectorate... Information on the admission and the admission procedure will be found on the website of the Free University of Bozen-Bolzano').

THE LANGUAGE GATE IS A HARD KNOCK-OUT AND IS ACTUALLY ENFORCED: failure to prove B2 means exclusion from the admission procedure regardless of grade. In the 2026/27 Early Bird EU round, two applicants (IDs 153130 and 153519) were listed under 'The following persons do not meet the language requirements for admission and are therefore excluded from the admission procedure. They may re-apply in the second session.' That is roughly 5% of the EU applicant pool lost on language alone — in a round that was otherwise under-subscribed, meaning those candidates would almost certainly have been admitted had their language evidence been in order.

B2 IS THE FLOOR, C1 IS THE SMART TARGET: a C1-or-better certificate adds 3 points to the ranking score, and at the 2026/27 non-EU cut-off of 68 those 3 points were exactly the margin.

WHERE TO PROVE IT: in the Application Portal, sections 'upload language certificates' and/or 'enrol for language exams', which become available only AFTER creating an application under 'create/manage applications'.

ADMINISTRATIVE FORM: 'In case your final certificate has been awarded by an Italian public institution, you need to submit a self-declaration. In case your final certificate has been awarded by a foreign public institution, you need to upload diploma scanned copy of the original.'

DEADLINE MECHANICS: certificates that cannot be uploaded 'can be sent by e-mail as PDF files or delivered in person to the Language Centre by the application deadline'.

SEPARATE, NON-BINDING SECOND-YEAR CONSIDERATION: Innsbruck offers part of the year-2 elective menu in German or Italian. No CEFR level is required for any of it, but German improves the range of electives and daily life in Innsbruck. unibz's Language Centre courses are available on a voluntary basis.
entry_levels_by_position:
ENGLISH B2 / no second language / no third language — in unibz's positional notation, B2 / none / none.

unibz expresses language requirements by POSITION (1st, 2nd, 3rd teaching language) rather than by named language. EMMA has only ONE teaching language, English, in first position, required at B2. No level is required in a second or third language at any stage, because the programme is not trilingual.

COMPARISON ACROSS UNIBZ, to place this correctly: trilingual bachelors run B2/B2/none (Bachelor in Computer Science) or B2/B1/none (Bachelor in Electronic and Information Engineering); trilingual masters in Economics run C1/B2/none (Master in Public Policy and Innovative Governance, Master in Accounting and Finance). Against those, EMMA's single B2-in-English entry level is the least demanding language profile available at unibz, tied with the other fully English-taught masters such as Energy Engineering and Software Engineering.

THE ONE NUANCE UNIQUE TO EMMA AMONG THE ENGLISH-ONLY MASTERS: because year 2 is delivered by a German-speaking partner university, the SECOND language (German) has real practical weight in year 2 even though it carries no formal level requirement — for the elective menu at the Innsbruck Faculty of Biology and for life in Innsbruck. This is a soft, self-managed factor, not a position in unibz's requirement grid.
exit_levels:
NO EXIT / GRADUATION LANGUAGE REQUIREMENT. Neither the 2026/27 admission-information PDF, nor the brochure, nor the signed ranking list states any exit level; the entire 'Language requirements' section is headed 'Entry level (to gain admission)' and covers admission only.

This places EMMA on the English-taught side of unibz's two-model system. The unibz Study Guide's C1/C1/B1 graduation model — 'in order to graduate, you will need to certify two languages at the C1 level and the third language at the B1 level' — applies to TRILINGUAL master programmes. An entirely English-taught master 'does not include language requirements in other languages', with Language Centre courses offered as an optional extra.

PRACTICAL SIGNIFICANCE: this removes the single biggest hidden risk of studying at unibz for an international student. In the trilingual programmes, students routinely gain admission and then cannot graduate on time because they have not certified the second and third languages. In EMMA, once admitted with B2 English, no further language certification stands between the student and the degree — including in Innsbruck, where the compulsory module and the thesis are in English and the thesis may be defended at either university.

HISTORICAL CURIOSITY: the 2019/20 study plan included a compulsory 3 CP course 'Scientific English (C1-level)' in the first year. That course has disappeared from the current study plan, so even the internal English-progression element is gone.

Students may still voluntarily take German or Italian at the unibz Language Centre, which is worth doing for the South Tyrol/Tyrol job market and for the Innsbruck year, but it carries no graduation consequence.
third_language_exam_threshold:
NOT APPLICABLE — there is no second or third teaching language, therefore no third-language B1 threshold.

The rule this field is designed to capture — a B1 level in the third language required from the second semester of the first year in order to be allowed to sit exams — belongs exclusively to unibz's TRILINGUAL programmes. It does not appear in the EMMA 2026/27 admission-information PDF, brochure or signed ranking list, and it cannot apply to a programme whose 'official teaching language is English' full stop. There is likewise no first- or second-language exam threshold gating exam attendance at any point in the two years.

The only language condition attached to EMMA is the B2 English entry gate, which is settled before admission and never revisited. The unibz Study Guide page that governs this programme is 'English-taught master programmes', not 'Trilingual master programmes'.

No German or Italian threshold arises in year 2 either: Innsbruck imposes no language condition on EMMA students, since admission and enrolment are handled by unibz under the cooperation agreement.
proof_pathways:
FOUR RECOGNISED WAYS TO PROVE ENGLISH B2 (admission-information PDF, verbatim numbering):

(1) MEDIUM OF INSTRUCTION AT HIGH SCHOOL — 'the main teaching language in your final high school year, if English (recognised as C1). Foreign qualifications: If the main teaching language is not clearly stated on your high school diploma, please also upload a letter/document issued by your high school stating the medium of instruction.' Recognised at C1, so it ALSO earns the 3-point bonus.

(2) A DEGREE TAUGHT IN ENGLISH — 'a bachelor or master degree in English (recognised as C1). unibz graduates must upload the language certificates obtained and/or declare that they have passed language exams at the unibz Language Centre (B2, B2+ or C1). Foreign qualifications: If the teaching language is not clearly stated on your University degree, please also upload a letter/document issued by your University stating the medium of instruction during your studies.' Also recognised at C1, so also worth the 3 points. THIS IS THE HIGHEST-VALUE, LOWEST-COST ROUTE FOR A TURKISH APPLICANT: graduates of 100%-English-medium Turkish programmes (e.g. METU, Boğaziçi, ITU English-track, Bilkent, Koç, Sabancı, and the English-medium Orman/Ziraat Fakültesi tracks) should request a formal medium-of-instruction letter from the registrar, because Turkish diplomas almost never state the language. Applicants from 30%-English Turkish programmes must NOT rely on this route — unibz asks for the medium of instruction 'during your studies', and a partial-English programme will not satisfy it.

(3) A RECOGNISED LANGUAGE CERTIFICATE from the official unibz list. 'If you cannot upload the certificates, you can send them by e-mail as PDF files or deliver them in person to the Language Centre by the application deadline.'

(4) A UNIBZ LANGUAGE CENTRE EXAM — 'You can register for these exams online through the application portal (in the section "enrol for language exams") after you have filled out your application in the section "create/manage applications".' Held ONLINE. 2026/27 sittings and registration windows — Early Bird: exam 16/03/2026 (registration 02–09/03/2026) and exams 16–17 and 20–21/04/2026 (registration 24/03–08/04/2026); Late: exams 22–26/06/2026 (registration 28/05–15/06/2026) and 27/07/2026 (registration 10–19/07/2026). PROCEDURAL TRAP, verbatim: 'If you start your application outside a language exams registration period, you must return to the portal during one of the periods indicated above in order to register for an exam.' Information on the structure, duration and results-processing time of the proficiency exams is published on the Language Centre pages.

RECOMMENDATION SPECIFIC TO EMMA: routes (1) and (2) are strictly superior to (3) and (4), because they are recognised AS C1 and therefore automatically deliver the 3 ranking points, whereas a certificate at exactly B2 satisfies the gate but scores zero on the bonus. Given that the 2026/27 non-EU cut-off was 68 = base 65 + the 3-point C1 bonus, this choice was literally decisive for at least one applicant.

CAUTIONARY EVIDENCE: two EU applicants were excluded outright on language grounds in the 2026/27 Early Bird round in an otherwise under-subscribed session. Language evidence, not academic merit, was what cost them the place.
certificate_rules:
Governed by the unibz list of recognised language certificates (Resolution of the University Council no. 16/2026, 'Recognised language certificates and diplomas — Students and applicants'), a university-wide document that applies to EMMA unchanged. Full list: https://www.unibz.it/assets/Documents/Languages/unibz-recognised-language-certificates-v2.pdf (verified HTTP 200 on 2026-08-29).

B2 ENGLISH EQUIVALENCES — the level EMMA requires: IELTS (General and Academic) 5.5–6.5; TOEFL iBT 72–94; Cambridge B2 First (FCE) grade B or C, and B2 First for Schools; Cambridge B1 Business Preliminary / BEC Vantage grade B or C; TOEIC Listening 400+, Reading 385+, Speaking 160+, Writing 150+; PTE Academic 43–58; PTE General Level 3; PEIC B2; LanguageCert General B2 / LanguageCert Academic B2 / LanguageCert ESOL B2; Michigan English Test (MET) B2 (all four skills); Aptis ESOL General B2 and Aptis ESOL Advanced B2.

C1 EQUIVALENCES — the level that triggers EMMA's 3-point bonus: IELTS 7.0–8.0; TOEFL iBT 95–113; Cambridge C1 Advanced (CAE); BEC Higher grade B/C; TOEIC Listening 490+, Reading 455+, Speaking 180+, Writing 180+; PTE Academic 59–75; LanguageCert C1; MET C1; Aptis ESOL Advanced C1. C2: IELTS 8.5+, TOEFL iBT 114–120, Cambridge C2 Proficiency (CPE), ECPE, PEIC C2, PTE Academic 85–90.

GENERAL RULES: (1) the certificate must assess ALL FOUR SKILLS and be issued by the certification organisation itself; (2) an overall grade must be shown, or the detailed per-skill assessment must appear on the certificate or in documentation from the issuer; (3) if no overall level is stated, THE LOWEST LEVEL REACHED IN ANY SUB-SKILL determines the recognised level; (4) there is NO COMPENSATION between skills and no averaging unless the issuer itself provides it — this matters directly for the EMMA bonus, since a candidate with three C1 sub-scores and one B2 sub-score is recognised at B2 and loses the 3 points; (5) 'Certificates regarding single skills issued by different certification organisations will not be accepted'; (6) certificates of participation, end-of-course tests, exams from private educational institutions, placement-test results and certificates issued by individual lecturers are NOT recognised; (7) DAAD certificates are NOT recognised.

HOME EDITION: online 'home edition' exams are generally NOT recognised, EXCEPT those explicitly asterisked in the list. For English the asterisk ('Also accepted as "home edition"') covers TOEFL, TOEIC, IELTS (General and Academic) and LanguageCert Academic — a significant practical advantage for candidates in Türkiye and other countries where at-home testing is widespread.

VALIDITY: 'International language certificates must not be older than five years before the date of their submission. The entire calendar year shall apply from 1 January.' Items under 'Further Recognised Degrees, Diplomas and Certificates' — which is where an English-medium degree or high-school diploma sits — have UNLIMITED validity. This is a further reason to prefer the medium-of-instruction route over a certificate: it never expires and it counts as C1.
application_deadline_eu:
THREE POSSIBLE SESSIONS for EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment; two were actually opened for 2026/27. All closing times are noon (12:00) local Italian time. Dates normalised to ISO; unibz writes DD/MM/YYYY.

EARLY BIRD APPLICATION — 2026-03-02 to 2026-04-28 (unibz: 'Application: 02/03 - 28/04/2026 (by noon local time)'). This is also the ONLY window open to non-EU citizens living abroad. Language exams within this session: 2026-03-16 (registration 2026-03-02 to 2026-03-09) and 2026-04-16/17 and 2026-04-20/21 (registration 2026-03-24 to 2026-04-08).

LATE APPLICATION (EU citizens only) — 2026-05-28 to 2026-08-20 (unibz: 'Application: 28/05 - 20/08/2026 (by noon local time)'). Language exams: 2026-06-22 to 2026-06-26 (registration 2026-05-28 to 2026-06-15) and 2026-07-27 (registration 2026-07-10 to 2026-07-19). This session was genuinely worth entering in 2026/27, because the Early Bird round admitted only 31 against 35 EU places, and the rollover rule sends the 4 unfilled places into the Late round on top of its own 10 — up to 14 EU places. Verbatim on re-applying: 'You might apply for more than one study programme. If you are excluded in the first session, you might apply again in the second one', and the ranking list tells both the below-threshold and the language-failed candidates 'They may re-apply in the second session.'

ADDITIONAL APPLICATION SESSION (EU citizens only) — no fixed dates. Verbatim: 'The Faculty can open additional application sessions for single study programmes in August and in September if there are available places. More information on additional sessions will be published in due course.' STATUS AS OF 2026-08-29: no Additional Session for EMMA appears on the unibz ranking-lists index.

HARD RULE: 'Once the application has been sent, it cannot be modified. Filled-in forms which have not been sent correctly will not be taken into consideration.'

[uncertain] 2027/28 dates are not yet published. unibz has opened Early Bird in early March in recent cycles, so a 2027/28 applicant should plan for roughly March–April 2027 and watch the programme page from January 2027. Note that the EMMA calendar has been stable but the QUOTAS have grown materially over time (30 EU + 5 non-EU in 2019/20 → 45 EU + 8 non-EU in 2026/27), so next-cycle numbers may differ again.
application_deadline_non_eu:
ONE WINDOW ONLY, NO SECOND CHANCE: 2026-03-02 to 2026-04-28 (Early Bird), by noon local Italian time on the closing day. Verbatim: 'Non-EU-Citizens (living outside of Italy): Only one application period is offered. After the deadline it is not possible to apply anymore. Application fee: € 50.'

This is the single most important planning fact for a Turkish, Indian, Iranian, Pakistani, Nepali or other non-EU applicant who does not hold a qualifying Italian residence permit: miss 28 April and the academic year is gone. There is no Late Application and no Additional Session for this category — the Late round is headed 'only for EU citizens', and the ranking list's second sheet is headed 'NON-EU CITIZENS LIVING ABROAD' for Early Bird only.

DOWNSTREAM DEADLINES for a successful non-EU applicant in 2026/27: ranking list by 2026-05-27 (in practice signed and dated 2026-05-22); first instalment of EUR 600 to secure the place by 2026-06-05 noon; waiting-list call-ups from 2026-06-08; Universitaly pre-enrolment immediately after payment (mandatory); visa application at the Italian consulate; enrolment 2026-07-10 to 2026-10-13 noon. The gap between securing the place in early June and the October enrolment deadline is the visa window, and it is tight — Italian consulates in high-demand countries book out months ahead, so the Universitaly pre-enrolment should be filed the same week the instalment is paid.

EMMA-SPECIFIC EXTRA STEP, easily overlooked: because YEAR 2 IS IN AUSTRIA, a non-EU student must plan a SECOND immigration process about twelve months after arriving in Italy (see non_eu_visa_process). Nothing in the unibz application calendar prompts this.

WARNING ON CATEGORY ASSIGNMENT: 'if you do not upload the permit in the application portal, you will be automatically considered a non-EU citizen living abroad' — see parity_of_treatment.

GOOD NEWS ON COMPETITION: unlike most unibz masters, the non-EU EMMA round is only mildly oversubscribed — 8 places, 8 admitted, 1 on the waiting list in 2026/27 (see places_quotas).
parity_of_treatment:
TWO CATEGORIES ARE TREATED EXACTLY LIKE EU APPLICANTS. Verbatim from the admission-information PDF, under 'EU-Citizens and equivalent — Considered as equivalent are': '1. Citizens from Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Switzerland, San Marino and the Vatican City State; 2. Non-EU citizens with a valid permit to stay in Italy (see article 39, paragraph 5 of decree no. 286 of 25.07.1998: "permesso di soggiorno" (residence permit) for work, family reasons, political or humanitarian asylum, religious reasons). In this case, you apply directly to the University as described above and must submit a copy of your valid permit to stay. A permit to stay for study reasons or a visa for tourism is not valid. If the permit has expired, you must attach a renewal request.'

WHY THIS MATTERS ENORMOUSLY FOR TURKISH APPLICANTS: category 2 is the third route that converts a Turkish citizen from the 8-place, single-window, EUR 50-fee, visa-dependent non-EU track onto the 45-place EU track with TWO application windows and no application fee. A Turkish national already living in Italy on a work, family-reunification, asylum or religious permit qualifies. A Turkish national on a STUDENT permit — for example someone currently doing an Italian bachelor, including at unibz — does NOT. This is the most common and most damaging misunderstanding among Turkish applicants.

THE AUTOMATIC-DOWNGRADE TRAP, verbatim: 'Please note that if you do not upload the permit in the application portal, you will be automatically considered a non-EU citizen living abroad and therefore subject to the admission procedure through the Italian authorities in your country of origin.' The signed ranking list repeats it in enforcement language: 'If you have declared to be resident in Italy but have not attached to your application a copy of your valid residence permit for Italy (see article 39, paragraph 5 of decree no. 286 of 25.07.1998) you are ranked together with the non-EU citizen resident abroad.'

CONCRETE 2026/27 IMPACT, and it is smaller than at most unibz programmes: the EU/parity Early Bird list had 35 places and only 31 admissions — the track did not fill — while the non-EU list had 8 places, 8 admissions and 1 waiting-list candidate. So parity status in 2026/27 meant near-certain admission if eligible, versus a cut-off of 68/95 on the non-EU side. Parity status also unlocks the Late Application session and saves the EUR 50 fee.
places_quotas:
53 PLACES IN TOTAL for 2026/27. Brochure 'At a glance' and the programme page: 'Places available: 45 EU + 8 non-EU'. Broken down by session in the admission-information PDF, verbatim: 'EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment — Early Bird Application: 35; Late Application: 10. Non-EU citizens (living abroad) — Early Bird Application: 8.' So: EU Early Bird 35 / EU Late 10 / non-EU 8 (Early Bird only). The 45 is the EU TOTAL across the two sessions, not an Early Bird figure.

ROLLOVER RULE, verbatim: 'For EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment only: any remaining places of the early bird application, will be offered in the late application.' Unused non-EU places do not roll over to EU applicants under any published rule, and vice versa.

2026/27 OUTCOMES — THE REAL COMPETITION PICTURE (from the signed Early Bird ranking list of 22/05/2026):

EARLY BIRD, EU/PARITY: 31 admitted against 35 places — THE SESSION DID NOT FILL. No waiting list was published, because there was no need for one. Every applicant who cleared eligibility, the language gate and the 55/95 threshold was admitted; the lowest admitted score was 65/95. Exclusions were only: 2 applicants below the minimum score (IDs 151957, 152184), 2 for failing the language requirement (153130, 153519), and 2 for not meeting the admission requirements (151889, 152526). Total EU pool therefore about 37 applicants for 35 places, with 4 places rolling into the Late session.

EARLY BIRD, NON-EU LIVING ABROAD: exactly 8 admitted for 8 places (scores 88, 83, 78, 78, 78, 78, 78, 68) plus a 1-person waiting list at rank 9 (score 68). So at least 9 eligible non-EU applicants chased 8 places — an oversubscription of roughly 1.13x, with an effective cut-off of 68/95 decided by the tie-break at 68. Waiting-list candidates 'will be contacted by e-mail as of 8 June 2026 in case a spot opens up.'

required_documents:
UPLOADED IN THE APPLICATION PORTAL (https://aws.unibz.it/exup) AT APPLICATION — a short list by unibz standards, only three items plus ID:

(1) A VALID ID CARD OR PASSPORT, front and back, at account creation — 'if your document is invalid, incomplete or unreadable, you will be excluded from the admission procedure'.

(2) QUALIFICATION DOCUMENTS. Graduated in Italy: diploma supplement or a D.P.R. 445/2000 self-declaration of the degree with final grade and passed exams; if not yet graduated, a certificate listing the exams passed. Graduated abroad: diploma supplement or final degree certificate with the passed exams; if not yet graduated, a transcript of records — 'in Italian, German or English'. Mandatory contents: 'final grade, passed exams with indication of grade and date of passing, credit points, scientific fields (the latter only for Italian titles)'. FOR FOREIGN QUALIFICATIONS ADDITIONALLY: 'scale of grades awarded by the university of provenance (with a minimum final grade to obtain the qualification and a maximum final grade achievable)' — indispensable here, because the entire ranking score is computed from the grade. Also, if the qualification was gained abroad, the DIPLOMA itself must be uploaded ('if you are not yet in possession of the diploma, you'll need to upload it upon enrolment').

(3) THE EXCEL FILE — 'Please use the file available in the application portal.' The structured study-career template in which the applicant maps their exams onto the L-25 credit sectors, so the Committee can verify the 20 + 30 ECTS thresholds.

(4) ENGLISH LANGUAGE CERTIFICATIONS 'at least of level B2' — or medium-of-instruction documentation, or registration for a Language Centre exam. Italian public-institution certificates: self-declaration. Foreign public-institution certificates: scanned copy of the original.

(5) FOR PARITY-OF-TREATMENT APPLICANTS: a copy of the valid Italian permesso di soggiorno (or the renewal request if expired) — without it the applicant is automatically ranked as non-EU abroad.

NOT REQUIRED (and worth stating, because applicants over-prepare): no CV, no motivation letter, no reference letters, no research or thesis proposal, no portfolio, no video presentation, no GRE/GMAT score, no interview.

ADDITIONALLY AT ENROLMENT, FOR FOREIGN DEGREES: 'the degree diploma of your Bachelor; the official translation of your degree into Italian (translation is not necessary if the documents have been issued in German or English); the Diploma supplement, where it must be indicated: that you have achieved at least 180 credit points (ECTS) and that the qualification gives access to a Master programme' — plus the ARDI/CIMEA statements described under credential_recognition. Transfer students from another Italian university 'must submit to the Student Office - at the beginning of the academic year - a copy of the transfer application presented at the university of provenance'.

ADVISED THOUGH NOT LISTED: syllabi and course descriptions, since 'The Faculty reserves the right to request a description of the contents of the courses and/or teaching hours where necessary', and since the L-25 sector mapping for a foreign degree is judged 'based on the contents of the exams'.

EUR 1,200 PER YEAR IN TOTAL, paid to unibz in two instalments, for BOTH years — including the year spent in Austria. So the fee for the Innsbruck year is nominally handled through unibz and the student does not pay Austrian tuition twice. [uncertain] BUT THIS IS NOT FULLY WATERTIGHT: Austrian public universities levy a mandatory ÖH (student union) contribution on everyone enrolled — currently about EUR 25 per semester — and charge non-EU degree students a standard tuition of EUR 726.72 per semester (EUR 363.36 for certain categories) unless exempt. Third-party Austrian study portals list exactly these figures against EMMA. Neither unibz nor Innsbruck states on the EMMA pages whether double-degree students are exempt from the Austrian tuition, whether the ÖH contribution is additionally payable, or under what legal basis. FOR A NON-EU (e.g. TURKISH) APPLICANT THIS IS A POTENTIAL EUR 1,453 PER YEAR DIFFERENCE and must be confirmed in writing with the degree course director before accepting a place.

The first instalment is also the payment that SECURES an admitted place (Early Bird 2026/27 deadline 2026-06-05 noon; Late 2026-09-11 noon).

scholarships_grants:
NO PROGRAMME-SPECIFIC SCHOLARSHIP is published for EMMA. The available routes are university-wide, provincial or national, and one of them is complicated by the Austrian year.

(1) PROVINCIAL STUDY GRANT of the Autonomous Province of Bozen-Bolzano, administered by the Office for the Right to Study and applied for annually through the provincial e-government portal, with help from the South Tyrolean Students Association. Three instruments: ordinary study grants, merit scholarships, and 'grants for fostering postgraduate studies'. Grant holders also 'receive the reimbursement of monies paid for the academic year', i.e. the EUR 1,200 tuition comes back.

CRITICAL RESTRICTION FOR INTERNATIONAL STUDENTS, verbatim: non-EU students can apply 'only if they have a long-time residence permit or after they have had their residence in South Tyrol for at least one year without interruption'. A newly arrived non-EU first-year student is therefore effectively INELIGIBLE IN YEAR ONE and should budget accordingly.

AN EMMA-SPECIFIC TRAP FOLLOWS FROM THAT, and it is serious: the eligibility clock requires one uninterrupted year of residence in SOUTH TYROL, but EMMA students LEAVE South Tyrol for Austria exactly when that year is up. A non-EU student would become eligible in principle just as they cease to be resident in the province. [uncertain] Whether an EMMA student in the Innsbruck year retains provincial-grant eligibility, and how residence is assessed during that year, is NOT addressed anywhere on unibz.it. This should be asked of study@unibz.it before relying on provincial funding for year 2.

(2) UNIBZ TUITION-FEE EXEMPTIONS rather than cash: disability under Law 104/1992 art. 3(1) or ≥66% disability; holders of an Italian government scholarship.

(3) ITALIAN GOVERNMENT SCHOLARSHIPS for foreign students (the annual MAECI call and 'Invest Your Talent in Italy') — external to unibz, applied for separately, typically in the spring.

(4) AUSTRIAN AND GERMAN STUDENT SUPPORT PROGRAMMES are explicitly listed among the further funding sources on the unibz study-grants page — of particular potential relevance to EMMA because of the Innsbruck year, though eligibility for Austrian Studienbeihilfe is normally tied to Austrian residence or EU status. [uncertain]

(5) Other listed sources: Municipality of Meran-Merano scholarships (restricted to Food and Enogastronomy Sciences students, so NOT available to EMMA students) and Italian bank student-loan programmes.

[uncertain] The frequently cited provincial grant range of roughly EUR 1,680–6,960 per year and merit thresholds such as a 27/30 weighted average after the first year could NOT be confirmed on the pages verified for this programme; amounts and thresholds are set annually by the provincial call and must be checked directly.

credential_recognition:
AT ENROLMENT, a holder of a foreign bachelor degree must upload: 'the degree diploma of your Bachelor; the official translation of your degree into Italian (translation is not necessary if the documents have been issued in German or English); the Diploma supplement, where it must be indicated: that you have achieved at least 180 credit points (ECTS) and that the qualification gives access to a Master programme.' Then, depending on the education system:

(a) EU COUNTRIES, SWITZERLAND, NORWAY, ICELAND, LIECHTENSTEIN — 'the Statement of Correspondence of your Bachelor degree, to be downloaded from the ARDI - Automatic Recognition Database – Italy'.

(b) NON-EU COUNTRIES THAT ARE SIGNATORIES TO THE LISBON CONVENTION — BOTH the ARDI Statement of Correspondence AND 'the Statement of Verification of your Bachelor degree, issued by the Italian Information Centre on Academic Mobility and Equivalence (CIMEA)'.

(c) NON-EU COUNTRIES NOT SIGNATORIES TO THE LISBON CONVENTION — BOTH 'the Statement of Comparability of your Bachelor degree, issued by CIMEA' AND 'the Statement of Verification of your Bachelor degree, issued by CIMEA'.

FOR TURKISH APPLICANTS: Türkiye IS a signatory of the Lisbon Recognition Convention, so Turkish degrees normally fall under case (b) — ARDI Statement of Correspondence PLUS CIMEA Statement of Verification. Both take weeks and CIMEA charges a fee, so the process should start the moment the ranking list is published (late May for Early Bird) rather than near the October enrolment deadline.

RESERVATION AND REVOCATION: 'Your admission will be under reservation until the above-mentioned documents are uploaded. During enrolment, unibz verifies your foreign qualification and may request additional documents if necessary. If the access title is deemed eligible, the reservation will be lifted. Otherwise, enrolment will not be possible and you will be excluded.' And: 'Please note that if you do not possess a valid admission qualification, you can be excluded with Rector's decree even after enrolment.' Also: 'unibz performs the necessary checks on your foreign qualification and in case of doubt reserves the right to request additional documents.'

SEPARATELY, AT ADMISSION (not enrolment), the ACADEMIC CONTENT of a foreign degree is judged by the Admission Committee itself against the L-25 credit sectors: 'The correspondence of credit points awarded abroad to scientific-disciplinary sectors will be based on the contents of the exams. Please contact the degree course director in case you graduated abroad.' ARDI/CIMEA statements do NOT substitute for this content assessment, which is driven by the mandatory Excel file and, if requested, by course descriptions.

RECOGNITION OF PRIOR CREDITS: 'Credit points from previous university studies can only be recognised after enrolment if the exams taken at the university of provenance are equivalent in content to those offered at unibz.'

[uncertain] Nothing is published about whether the Austrian side performs its own recognition check when the student moves to Innsbruck for year 2, or whether unibz's assessment carries over automatically under the cooperation agreement.

non_eu_visa_process:
SEQUENCE FOR A NON-EU CITIZEN LIVING ABROAD (2026/27 dates), FOLLOWED BY AN EMMA-ONLY SECOND STEP THAT NO OTHER UNIBZ MASTER HAS:

PART A — ITALY, FOR YEAR 1:
(1) Apply to unibz in the EARLY BIRD WINDOW ONLY, 2026-03-02 to 2026-04-28 noon, paying the EUR 50 application fee. There is no second window.
(2) Appear on the SEPARATE NON-EU RANKING LIST (8 places), published by 2026-05-27.
(3) SECURE THE PLACE by paying the EUR 600 first instalment by 2026-06-05 noon.
(4) THEN PRE-ENROL ON UNIVERSITALY — mandatory and sequenced after payment. Verbatim: 'Once the ranking list has been published, if you have gained admission, secure it by paying the first instalment and then start your visa application on the Universitaly portal. The application on Universitaly is mandatory, otherwise you will not be allowed to enrol. On Universitaly you can apply for one study programme only.' The ranking list is blunter: 'Should you not follow this procedure, your direct online application to unibz will be declared null and void.'
(5) OBTAIN THE STUDY VISA from the Italian embassy/consulate. Explicit caveat: 'preliminary admission by unibz does not guarantee obtaining a visa, the issuing of which is the exclusive responsibility of embassies and consulates. Likewise, obtaining a visa for study purposes does not confer any right to perfecting the enrolment in a study programme.'
(6) ENROL ONLINE between 2026-07-10 and 2026-10-13 noon.
(7) AFTER ARRIVAL: 'within 8 working days of your arrival in Italy, according to Italian law you must apply for a residence permit'; contact Student Support/Advisory Service immediately. Once the permesso di soggiorno is issued, hand it in at the Student Office.

ITALIAN RESIDENCE-PERMIT PRACTICALITIES (from the unibz Study Guide's non-EU page): costs are a EUR 16 duty stamp, EUR 30 insured post, EUR 30.46 electronic permit issuance and EUR 40 for a permit of 90 days to 1 year; medical insurance covering illness and accidents is mandatory and must match the permit's validity (the Welcome Association Italy option costs about EUR 81 for 6 months or EUR 130 for 12 months; full national health service registration costs about EUR 700 per year, valid January–December); a housing contract or owner's declaration is required. RENEWAL: apply at least 60 days before expiry; for the first renewal you must have 'passed at least one exam', and from the second renewal at least two exams per year; renewal requires evidence of at least EUR 7,954 in funds; renewals are possible up to the 3rd year after the normal programme length (5 years total for a master). WORK: 'maximum 20 hours per week' with 'an annual limit of 1,040 hours'.

PART B — AUSTRIA, FOR YEAR 2. THIS IS THE BIGGEST UNDOCUMENTED RISK IN THE WHOLE PROGRAMME. [uncertain] After year 1 the student moves to Innsbruck for a full academic year. Neither unibz's EMMA pages, nor unibz's non-EU guide, nor the University of Innsbruck's EMMA pages say ANYTHING about what a non-EU student must do to live and study legally in Austria for that year — no mention of an Austrian residence permit or visa D, no mention of intra-EU student mobility, no mention of who files what and when, no mention of health-insurance portability, and no mention of what happens to the Italian permesso di soggiorno while the holder is resident in Austria. The applicable legal framework is EU Directive (EU) 2016/801, which allows a third-country student holding a valid residence permit issued by one Member State to carry out part of their studies in a second Member State (as a rule for up to 360 days) under a notification procedure between the two national authorities, provided the mobility is part of a Union or multilateral programme or an agreement between the institutions — which an inter-institutional double-degree agreement such as EMMA's would normally satisfy. But this is a general legal reading, NOT a statement published by either university, and the notification is time-consuming and must be initiated well in advance. Additional open questions: whether the Italian permit can be renewed while the student is in Austria (renewal requires exams passed, which in year 2 are Austrian exams), and whether time in Austria breaks the continuous-Italian-residence requirements that matter for the provincial study grant and for long-term residence status.

ACTION FOR A TURKISH APPLICANT: before accepting a place, obtain written answers from the degree course director and the Advisory Service (apply@unibz.it) on (i) the exact immigration route for the Innsbruck year, (ii) who initiates it and by when, (iii) whether the Italian permit is maintained and renewable throughout, and (iv) whether Austrian tuition and the ÖH contribution apply.

FINANCIAL MEANS FOR THE INITIAL ITALIAN VISA: proof of roughly EUR 800 per month of living costs excluding tuition, i.e. on the order of EUR 24,000 for a two-year master. [uncertain] — this figure comes from unibz general international-applicant material and Italian ministerial practice, not from the EMMA 2026/27 PDF; consulates set their own evidentiary standards, and an Austrian year may attract separate means-testing.

REFUND EXCEPTION: non-EU applicants abroad who pay the instalment but do not obtain the documents necessary for enrolment from the Italian authorities in their country ARE entitled to a refund — the only refund route unibz grants.

ADMISSION IS PROVISIONAL THROUGHOUT: 'All non-EU citizens living abroad are provisionally admitted: requirement is the official communication sent by the Italian consulate abroad directly to unibz.'
